ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, what component should be added within the dashed box to convert the D flip-flop into a T flip-flop?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure is a D flip-flop; the input terminal is labeled D, and the clock terminal is labeled C. At the lower left, CP is connected to the clock terminal. The dashed box on the left has a T input from the left, and the output of the dashed box is connected to the D input of the D flip-flop. On the right there are output Q and \bar{Q} with an inversion mark, and from the \bar{Q} terminal a feedback line connects back to another input of the dashed box. Reasoning: The characteristic equation of the D flip-flop is Q_next = D. A T flip-flop needs to satisfy Q_next = T ⊕ Q, that is, it holds when T=0 and toggles when T=1. Since the dashed box receives T and the feedback \bar{Q}, it must generate D = T ⊕ Q. Also because Q = NOT(\bar{Q}), T ⊕ Q = T ⊕ NOT(\bar{Q}) = T XNOR \bar{Q}. Therefore an XNOR gate should be added inside the dashed box.
